title: The Forest That Reads the River

features.name: the river rendered as text
features.desc-on-touch: Where the water enters the grove, syllables rise from the current. Each tributary adds its own dialect; the river speaks in the voices of every creek that fed it.

features.name: roots that remember rainfall
features.desc-on-touch: The root system here holds memories in soil chemistry. Each layer reads the sky of a different season. The tree is a chronicle grown downward into time.

features.name: the canopy's consonants
features.desc-on-touch: Where leaves click and whisper above, the spacing and silence between them follows the river's own grammar. Each branch ends a sentence; each gap begins one.

features.name: where stone learned to listen
features.desc-on-touch: Boulders in the stream are carved by water-speech into surfaces that echo back what they hear. The river reads itself in stone; the stone reads the river in erosion patterns.

features.name: the ferns that file everything
features.desc-on-touch: Fronds here unfurl like pages. Each fern is a catalogue of all the streams it has drunk. In their fronds you can read the history of every tributary.

features.name: the catalogue of all separate tributaries
features.desc-on-touch: A file listing that records each tributary separately—as if they could ever be filed apart. Yet their names are written on one card, in the order they converge.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the river that reads itself in two voices
narr: You sat on the stone bank while Leif read aloud
from something he'd copied: a passage about water.
Katita was upstream, not reading, just listening.
The river's dialect kept interrupting his words.
He stopped. She called back: what you cannot read,
the river remembers. He folded the paper then.

inscription: the river knew how to write before it knew how to flow; trees grow into the grammar of water
